listing_view.reasoning: Subscription went from ~1x on day one morning to ~34.7x by close of day three, with almost all of it arriving on the final day — that pattern signals strong listing pop potential but is largely window-dressing style demand, not a verdict on fundamentals. At ₹146 the implied P/E on weighted-average EPS (~8.68) is roughly 17x, not absurdly priced for 53% PAT growth, which leaves room for a first-day premium.

longterm_view.reasoning: Revenue growing ~21.5% CAGR with PAT margins expanding from 5% to ~8% and an order book of ₹79.5bn versus ₹36bn revenue (≈2.2 years of cover) is a decent EPC profile. But operating cash flow converted only 55% of PAT cumulatively — ₹2.1bn of cash against ₹6.3bn of three-year profit — and working capital stress is the classic killer of Indian EPC stories; the prospectus itself flags that order book revenue 'may be significantly less than estimates' [business, page 200]. Top-10 customer concentration tables are referenced but I was not given the numbers, so the quality of that revenue cannot be verified.

governance.reasoning: No material SEBI findings are disclosed [litigation, page 396] and promoters have given no material third-party guarantees [promoters, page 252], but the prospectus discloses an extensive related-party transaction footprint [promoters, page 317, page 332] with no figures given to me, so related-party risk is real but unquantifiable.

key_risks.why_it_matters: Only 55 paise of every ₹1 of reported profit arrived as cash, meaning earnings quality depends on receivables being collected from (likely government) clients.
